headline: High: CrewAI’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can conflict with Botpress outputs and create default-path data leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress can emit chatbot content that CrewAI may ingest through its shared working-directory and stdin/stdout surfaces. CrewAI’s shared-memory, tool-calling crew model makes instruction-like content more likely to be treated as actionable. No direct MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF CrewAI reads Botpress-generated files or messages as instructions without provenance checks
IF Botpress output is copied into a CrewAI task or shared workspace
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to Botpress outputs
Require CrewAI to ignore instructions inside retrieved content
Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic file ingestion in CrewAI
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is documented with no network egress, while CrewAI has broad egress, reads the filesystem, and handles API keys and developer-passed data. If they share a workspace, Botpress artifacts can be read and then transmitted by CrewAI to model providers or tools. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default CrewAI setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress writes sensitive conversation artifacts into a directory CrewAI can read
IF CrewAI forwards those artifacts to model providers or configured tools
mitigations: Store Botpress and CrewAI data in separate directories
Redact secrets before CrewAI reads files
Restrict CrewAI tool outputs from including raw file contents
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while CrewAI can execute shells, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses in the host working directory. Even though CrewAI cannot modify git state, overlapping write access to the same directory can still cause file clobbering or dependency drift. The conflict is real in default host-shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory
IF Botpress package installation changes files CrewAI also writes
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Pin dependencies for Botpress
Run CrewAI in a read-only mount for shared assets
Serialize writes with a lock file
requires-engineering: containerize each agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew and tool-use pattern can treat upstream outputs as task inputs, while Botpress produces customer-support responses that may be taken as authoritative. If CrewAI acts on Botpress-generated facts without verification, errors can cascade into downstream tool actions or model-provider calls. This is a default-path risk because CrewAI is built for autonomous orchestration.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses Botpress output as task context without a verification step
IF CrewAI triggers external tools or API calls based on that output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require citation checks on Botpress outputs
Constrain CrewAI tools to read-only mode
Add a confidence threshold before acting
requires-engineering: implement structured validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented data classes, while CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed data and API keys and can send data to model providers. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if support data or secrets flow from Botpress into CrewAI. The profiles do not document HIPAA/GDPR specifics, so I avoid stronger claims.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts or secrets are passed from Botpress into CrewAI
IF CrewAI’s provider or tool retention differs from Botpress’s handling
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Block secrets from CrewAI inputs
Review provider retention settings
Keep support data out of CrewAI unless necessary
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
